[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve using the **unit digit** method to quickly identify the answer.

Expression **unit digits**: 9 + 7 − (2 + 9) + 6 − 4 + 3

⇒ 9 + 7 − (1) + 6 − 4 + 3

⇒ 16 − 1 + 6 − 4 + 3 = 15 + 6 − 4 + 3 = 20

The **unit digit** of the result must be **0**. Among the options, only 130 ends with 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 130.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 89 + 47 − (32 + 19) + 76 − 54 + 23

Apply the **BODMAS** rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 89 + 47 − (51) + 76 − 54 + 23

Group the **positive** and **negative** terms together:

⇒ (89 + 47 + 76 + 23) − 51 − 54

⇒ 235 − (51 + 54)

⇒ 235 − 105

⇒ 130

**∴ The correct answer is 130.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It specifies the order of operations to solve expressions: **Brackets** (), **Orders** (powers/roots), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Grouping Method

In multi-step **addition and subtraction**, summing all positive numbers and all negative numbers separately before the final subtraction reduces calculation errors.

Unit Digit Check

This is a **verification shortcut** where only the last digits are calculated to match with the options, saving time during competitive exams.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **BODMAS**: 84 + 47 − 33 + (19 × 2) + 28 ÷ 4 − 16.

Solve **Brackets** and **Division**: 19 × 2 = 38 and 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

Group all **Positive** terms: 84 + 47 + 38 + 7 = 176.

Group all **Negative** terms: 33 + 16 = 49.

Final calculation: 176 − 49 = 127.

**∴ The correct answer is 127.**

questions.question: frac{sqrt{20} + sqrt{45}}{sqrt{5}} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distribute the **division** across the terms in the **numerator**: √(a+b) ÷ √c = √(a÷c) + √(b÷c).

⇒ √(20 ÷ 5) + √(45 ÷ 5)

⇒ √4 + √9 = 2 + 3 = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (√20 + √45) ÷ √5

**Method:** Factorize the **radicands** to identify **perfect squares**.

⇒ √20 = √(4 × 5) = 2√5

⇒ √45 = √(9 × 5) = 3√5

⇒ (√20 + √45) ÷ √5 = (2√5 + 3√5) ÷ √5

⇒ 5√5 ÷ √5

⇒ 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quotient Law of Surds

For any positive real numbers a and b, the **square root** of their quotient is the quotient of their square roots: √(a ÷ b) = √a ÷ √b.

Addition of Like Surds

Surds can be added or subtracted only if they are **like surds** (having the same number under the radical sign): m√x + n√x = (m + n)√x.

Simplifying Radicals

To simplify a **radical**, find the largest **perfect square** factor of the radicand and move its square root outside the radical: √(k² × a) = k√a.

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangle is 11 cm and 6 cm respectively. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Perimeter** of a rectangle = 2 × (**Length** + **Breadth**)

Sum of dimensions = 11 + 6 = 17 cm

Total **Perimeter** = 2 × 17 = 34 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of the rectangle (l) = 11 cm

**Breadth** of the rectangle (b) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Perimeter** of a rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e7b9ed2690dbac1a5442fcb8895b4a4c14a7aa3178d0963cea0e8919e9a2126d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Perimeter** = 2 × (11 + 6)

⇒ **Perimeter** = 2 × 17

⇒ **Perimeter** = 34 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total surface area enclosed by the rectangle is calculated as **Length × Breadth**.

Diagonal of Rectangle

The length of the **diagonal** (d) can be found using Pythagoras theorem: d = √(l² + b²).

Square Properties

A **square** is a special rectangle where length equals breadth (l = b = s). Its **Perimeter** is 4 × s and **Area** is s².

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 36 cm. The length of the rectangle is 10 cm. What is the breadth (in cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Semi-perimeter** (Length + Breadth) = **Perimeter** ÷ 2.

Semi-perimeter = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 cm.

**Breadth** = Semi-perimeter − **Length**.

Breadth = 18 − 10 = 8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** of the rectangle = 36 cm, **Length** = 10 cm.

**Formula:** **Perimeter** = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d26f9d3dddd1ab19fb61cfc450a6a400d5379b58daf3875bc4e6d77ae8c910de.png] 

⇒ 36 = 2 × (10 + Breadth)

⇒ 36 ÷ 2 = 10 + Breadth

⇒ 18 = 10 + Breadth

⇒ Breadth = 18 − 10

⇒ Breadth = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The space occupied by a rectangle is calculated as Length × Breadth.

Diagonal of Rectangle

The **diagonal** of a rectangle forms a right-angled triangle with the length and breadth; d = √(Length² + Breadth²).

Properties of Rectangle

Opposite sides are equal and parallel, and every internal angle is exactly 90°.

questions.question: ((173+258)² - (173-258)²)/(173 times 258) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **algebraic identity** in the expression: ((a + b)² − (a − b)²) / (ab).

The standard formula for the numerator is **(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab**.

Substituting this into the expression: 4ab / ab = 4.

The result is independent of the values of **173** and **258**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The expression is ((173 + 258)² − (173 − 258)²) / (173 × 258).

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

⇒ Let **a = 173** and **b = 258**.

⇒ The numerator is (a + b)² − (a − b)².

⇒ Expanding the terms: (a² + b² + 2ab) − (a² + b² − 2ab).

⇒ Simplifying: a² + b² + 2ab − a² − b² + 2ab.

⇒ All squared terms cancel out, leaving: 2ab + 2ab = 4ab.

⇒ Final expression = 4ab / ab.

⇒ Result = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

The identity (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) is often used in similar simplification problems.

Difference of Two Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is used when two squared numbers are subtracted.

Standard Algebraic Identity

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² is the most fundamental expansion in competitive algebra.

questions.question: 55 × (40² + 30² - 1300) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the bracketed **Squares** first: 40² = 1600 and 30² = 900.

Simplify the bracket sum and difference: 1600 + 900 − 1300 = 1200.

Perform the **Multiplication**: 55 × 1200 = 66000.

**∴ The correct answer is 66000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 55 × (40² + 30² − 1300)

The problem is solved using the **BODMAS Rule** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 55 × (1600 + 900 − 1300)

⇒ 55 × (2500 − 1300)

⇒ 55 × 1200

⇒ 66000

**∴ The correct answer is 66000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule Priority

Always prioritize operations inside **Brackets** before handling exponents (Orders) and basic arithmetic operations like **Addition** or **Multiplication**.

Shortcut for Squaring Numbers ending in Zero

To square a number ending in zero, square the base digits and append twice the number of zeros (e.g., 40² = 4² followed by 00 = 1600).

Multiplication by 55

Multiplying by 55 can be simplified as (50 + 5) × Number or 5 × 11 × Number to speed up mental **Calculation**.

questions.question: 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + ...... + 40³ = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of **cubes of first n natural numbers** is the square of their sum: [n(n + 1) / 2]².

Here, **n = 40**.

Sum = [40 × (40 + 1) / 2]² = [20 × 41]²

Sum = 820² = 672400.

**∴ The correct answer is 672400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The series is 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + ...... + 40³

This is a series of the **sum of cubes** of the first 40 natural numbers.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers (Sₙ) = [n(n + 1) / 2]²

**Calculations:**

⇒ n = 40

⇒ S₄₀ = [40 × (40 + 1) / 2]²

⇒ S₄₀ = [40 × 41 / 2]²

⇒ S₄₀ = [20 × 41]²

⇒ S₄₀ = (820)²

⇒ S₄₀ = 672400

**∴ The correct answer is 672400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum is given by the formula: Sₙ = n(n + 1) / 2.

Sum of Squares of First n Natural Numbers

The sum is given by the formula: Sₙ = n(n + 1)(2n + 1) / 6.

Sum of First n Even Numbers

The sum of the first n even natural numbers is calculated as: Sₙ = n(n + 1).

questions.question: Average of 14 numbers is 50. Average of 5 numbers among them is 'x'. Average of the remaining numbers is 45. What is the value of 'x'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the overall **average** of 50 as the baseline for all 14 numbers.

Deviation for 9 numbers = 9 × (45 − 50) = 9 × (−5) = −45.

To maintain the average, the remaining 5 numbers must have a total deviation of +45.

Deviation per number for 'x' = +45 ÷ 5 = +9.

Value of x = Baseline Average + Deviation = 50 + 9 = 59.

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total numbers = 14, Average of 14 numbers = 50, Number of first group = 5, Average of first group = x, Number of second group = 9, Average of second group = 45.

**Formula:** Total Sum = (n₁ × Avg₁) + (n₂ × Avg₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f143552ad5d3f64975d3941fac889666615a96e17c933fbf9dde027b8926d9f.png] 

⇒ Total Sum of 14 numbers = 14 × 50 = 700

⇒ Sum of the remaining 9 numbers = 9 × 45 = 405

⇒ Sum of the 5 numbers = Total Sum − Sum of 9 numbers

⇒ Sum of the 5 numbers = 700 − 405 = 295

⇒ Average of 5 numbers (x) = Sum ÷ Count = 295 ÷ 5

⇒ x = 59

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The average or mean is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations: Average = Σx ÷ n.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the resulting average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of the deviations of all individual values from the arithmetic mean is always zero. This is a powerful tool for finding missing averages.

questions.question: What is the Highest Common Factor of 20, 30 and 50?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is either the **smallest difference** between any two numbers or a factor of that difference.

Differences: 30 − 20 = **10** and 50 − 30 = 20.

Smallest difference = **10**.

Check if 10 divides all given numbers: 20 ÷ 10 = 2, 30 ÷ 10 = 3, and 50 ÷ 10 = 5.

Since 10 divides all numbers exactly, it is the **HCF**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

questions.question: Find the maximum number of students among whom 280 chips and 420 toffees can be distributed such that each student gets the same number of each.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **maximum number of students** for equal distribution, calculate the **HCF (Highest Common Factor)** of the given quantities.

Quantity 1 = 280 (Chips)

Quantity 2 = 420 (Toffees)

Difference Method: 420 − 280 = 140

Since 140 divides both 280 and 420 exactly, the HCF is 140.

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of **chips** = 280

Total number of **toffees** = 420

**Formula Used:**

Maximum number of students = **HCF** of (280, 420)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b926570da82559a2e89f9a0178624d678789b6e3d72371aa29d2505cde355be.png] 

**Calculations:**

Using **prime factorization** method:

⇒ 280 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 7 = 2³ × 5 × 7

⇒ 420 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ HCF = Product of the lowest powers of common factors

⇒ HCF = 2² × 5 × 7

⇒ HCF = 4 × 5 × 7

⇒ HCF = 140

Each student will get 280 ÷ 140 = 2 chips and 420 ÷ 140 = 3 toffees.

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without leaving a remainder. It is also known as **GCD (Greatest Common Divisor)**.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**.

HCF of Fractions

HCF of (a/b, c/d) = **HCF of Numerators (a, c) ÷ LCM of Denominators (b, d)**.

questions.question: 340 percent of 70 percent of 60 = ___ .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Strike out the **three zeros** in **340**, **70**, and **60** against the **percent** denominators.

Perform the remaining multiplication: 34 × 7 × 6 ÷ 10.

34 × 42 = 1428.

Divide by the remaining 10: 1428 ÷ 10 = 142.8.

**∴ The correct answer is 142.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **340 percent** of **70 percent** of **60**.

**Formula Used:** x% of y = (x ÷ 100) × y

⇒ Result = (340 ÷ 100) × (70 ÷ 100) × 60

⇒ Result = 3.4 × 0.7 × 60

⇒ Result = 3.4 × 42

⇒ Result = 142.8

**∴ The correct answer is 142.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Commutative Property of Percentage

The operation is commutative: **x% of y** is equal to **y% of x**, which can simplify mental math.

Decimal Conversion

To convert any **percentage** to a decimal, move the decimal point two places to the left (e.g., 340% = 3.4).

Successive Percentages

For calculations involving **a% of b% of c**, the combined multiplier is (a × b ÷ 10,000).

questions.question: Selling price of an article is Rs. 672. Profit percentage is 12 percent. What is the value of the profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit percentage** (12%) means if **Cost Price** is 100 units, **Selling Price** is 112 units.

Given 112 units → Rs. 672

1 unit → 672 ÷ 112 = 6

Value of **Profit** (12 units) → 12 × 6 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling Price** (SP) = Rs. 672

**Profit Percentage** (P%) = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = [P% ÷ (100 + P%)] × SP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/704a58612db2ab52f9aeaa76f02d8e34ff74040fd2e30d672bf8f02c6dae9ef7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = [12 ÷ (100 + 12)] × 672

⇒ Profit = (12 ÷ 112) × 672

⇒ Profit = 12 × (672 ÷ 112)

⇒ Profit = 12 × 6

⇒ Profit = 72

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Profit and Loss Formulas

**Profit** = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP). Profit only occurs when SP > CP.

Cost Price Formula

**Cost Price** = [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)] × SP. In this case, CP = [100 ÷ 112] × 672 = Rs. 600.

Profit Percentage

**Profit %** is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise: Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the loss of 10 percent. Cost price and selling price both are decreased by 20 percent. What will be the new loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** are both decreased or increased by the same percentage, the **profit or loss percentage** remains unchanged.

Since both CP and SP are decreased by an identical 20%, the initial loss of 10% will persist.

Ratio of SP to CP remains constant: 90 / 100 = 0.9.

New ratio = (90 × 0.8) / (100 × 0.8) = 72 / 80 = 0.9.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Loss Percentage** = 10%, **Reduction** in both CP and SP = 20%.

**Formula Used:** **Loss %** = [(CP − SP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce2714e57ec37782926cd909d8225832ab46a6891ad0400de755e054e8ef272d.png] 

⇒ Let the **initial CP** be 100 units.

⇒ **Initial SP** = 100 − 10% of 100 = 90 units.

⇒ **New CP** = 100 − 20% of 100 = 80 units.

⇒ **New SP** = 90 − 20% of 90 = 90 − 18 = 72 units.

⇒ **New Loss Amount** = New CP − New SP = 80 − 72 = 8 units.

⇒ **New Loss %** = (8 / 80) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and SP

When both CP and SP are multiplied or divided by the same factor (k), the **Profit** or **Loss percentage** remains constant because the ratio SP/CP remains unchanged.

Profit and Loss Formulas

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss / CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Selling Price Calculation

SP = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100 for loss and SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 for profit.

questions.question: A student scores total 80 percent marks in 3 subjects of 50 marks each. He scored 40 percent of total marks obtained by him, in subject 1. What is the score in subject 1?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total maximum marks = 3 × 50 = 150

Subject 1 score = 150 × 80% × 40%

Subject 1 score = 150 × 0.32 = 48 marks

**∴ The correct answer is 48 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of subjects = 3

Maximum marks per subject = 50

Aggregate percentage = 80%

Percentage of total marks in **Subject 1** = 40%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/647b62eabe40532d374ff520cf99c4a8bf362a4b13da9905506e959b9acdac11.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total maximum marks = 3 × 50 = 150

⇒ Total marks obtained = 80% of 150

⇒ Total marks obtained = (80 ÷ 100) × 150 = 120

⇒ Score in Subject 1 = 40% of 120

⇒ Score in Subject 1 = (40 ÷ 100) × 120 = 48 marks

**∴ The correct answer is 48 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Percentage Formula

Percentage = (Value ÷ Total Value) × 100. To find a value from a percentage: Value = (Percentage × Total) ÷ 100.

Fractional Conversions

Converting percentages to fractions speeds up calculations: 80% = 4/5 and 40% = 2/5.

Average Marks

Average marks = (Sum of marks in all subjects) ÷ (Number of subjects). In this case, Average = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 marks per subject.

questions.question: C is 5 times as efficient as D. C alone can do a work in 15 days. D alone can do 1/4 part of the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of **C : D** = 5 : 1.

Time ratio is inverse of efficiency, so **C : D** = 1 : 5.

Given 1 unit = **15 days**, then 5 units = 15 × 5 = **75 days** for **D**.

Time for **1/4 part** of work = 75 ÷ 4 = 18.75 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.75 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given that **C** is 5 times as efficient as **D** and **C** can complete the work in **15 days**.

Let efficiency of **D** = 1 unit/day.

Efficiency of **C** = 5 × 1 = 5 units/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = Efficiency of **C** × Time taken = 5 × 15 = 75 units.

 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

⇒ Days taken by **D** for full work = 75 ÷ 1 = 75 days.

⇒ Days taken by **D** for **1/4 part** of work = 75 × (1/4) = 18.75 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.75 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work (E ∝ 1/T).

Total Work Formula

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. This remains constant for the same piece of work.

Partial Work Calculation

Time for partial work = (Part of work to be done) × Total time taken for full work.

questions.question: A alone can do a work in 18 days. B alone can do the same work in 27 days. B alone started the work and worked for 9 days. In how many days A alone can finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Work** = LCM(18, 27) = 54 units.

**Efficiency** of A = 54 ÷ 18 = 3 units/day; Efficiency of B = 54 ÷ 27 = 2 units/day.

Work done by **B alone** in 9 days = 9 × 2 = 18 units.

Remaining work = 54 − 18 = 36 units.

Days taken by **A alone** to finish = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by A = 18 days; Time taken by B = 27 days; B worked for 9 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 18
 54
 3
 
 

 B
 27
 2
 
 

⇒ Work completed by **B** in 9 days = Efficiency of B × 9 days

⇒ Work done by **B** = 2 × 9 = 18 units

⇒ **Remaining Work** = Total Work − Work done by B

⇒ **Remaining Work** = 54 − 18 = 36 units

⇒ Time taken by **A** to finish remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If efficiency ratio is x : y, then time ratio is y : x for the same work.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed based on the **total work done** by each person. If they work for the same time, wages are proportional to efficiency.

Combined Work Formula

If two people finish work in A and B days, they finish together in (A × B) ÷ (A + B) days.

questions.question: A 240 metres long train takes 18 seconds to pass a stationary man. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find speed in **km/hr** directly: **Speed = (Length / Time) × (18/5)**

Speed = (240 / 18) × (18 / 5)

Speed = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the train (Distance) = 240 m

Time taken to pass the man = 18 sec

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1da71e474e052edb88d2609191e0b337866bac899ed1809e4d2706515eeac398.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed (in m/s) = 240 ÷ 18

⇒ Speed = 40/3 m/s

⇒ Speed (in km/hr) = (40/3) × (18/5)

⇒ Speed = (40 ÷ 5) × (18 ÷ 3)

⇒ Speed = 8 × 6

⇒ Speed = 48 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5. To convert from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Train Crossing a Platform

When a train crosses a stationary object with length (like a bridge or platform), total distance = **Length of Train + Length of Object**.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In the **opposite direction**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: A train crosses a standing pole in 10 seconds and a 400 metre long platform in 20 seconds. What is the length (in metres) and speed (in m/s) of the train?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Extra time taken to cross the **platform** = 20 − 10 = 10 sec. **Speed** of the **train** = Platform length ÷ Extra time = 400 ÷ 10 = 40 m/s. **Length** of the **train** = Speed × Pole crossing time = 40 × 10 = 400 m. **∴ The correct answer is 400 m, 40 m/s.**
